["In a case involving a posterior mediastinal mass (identified as pleomorphic liposarcoma), the source feedback highlighted a critical distinction in anatomical impact. While initial reasoning suggested displacement of the heart and trachea, the correct observation was that the mass caused compression of the right lung without significant tracheal or cardiac displacement. Post-surgical imaging confirmed re-expansion of the right lung while the heart and trachea remained in their original positions. This case illustrates that large posterior masses may compress adjacent lung parenchyma without shifting midline structures, a finding that contradicts the assumption that all significant mediastinal masses cause tracheal deviation. The final determination relied on recognizing the specific radiographic signs of malignancy (ill-defined/lobulated margins, effusions) rather than relying solely on automated classifier scores or generated text."]
